Thanks for sending, Suren — appreciate the quick turnaround. I reviewed the PDFs and the W-9 looks complete. A couple of follow-ups before procurement can clear the PO: 

1) EIN display mismatch: On the portal the name was entered as "GreyMatter AI" which triggers a DBA/name normalization check. Can you confirm the preferred invoicing name (legal name vs. DBA)? Our accounting system needs the legal name for the vendor record; invoices may carry the DBA but the PO must tie to the legal entity.

2) Signatory authority: We require a signatory attestation for payments over $50k. If the person who signed the bank letter is not an authorized signer, we need the authorization matrix or a short email from an officer confirming delegation.

3) Doc evidence: The bank letter is fine but procurement prefers a signed authorization matrix (spreadsheet) for faster routing. If you can place that in the portal we can avoid an extra DocuSign step.

Next steps from our side: I've looped in Kimberly (procurement) and Ben (tax onboarding) to validate the documents and run the EIN check. Kimberly — can you take a look at the bank letter and advise on whether we need DocuSign or if the matrix will suffice? Ben — can you run a quick EIN lookup against the IRS API and confirm match to the W-9?

If helpful I can create a mutual action plan in the portal with deadlines.

Best,
